items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: Implements exactly the ADR/mini-plan decision (advisory step + write-fresh + follow-up bot-PR step with stale-run guard); no extra scope.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Shell step guards both real failure branches explicitly (missing fresh-regen file, stale main head) and exits 0 with a ::notice:: rather than erroring; set -euo pipefail catches anything unhandled.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No user input in the shell body; only secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN via env; job-level permissions scoped to exactly contents:write + pull-requests:write, nothing wider; no new credential.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Tests assert on outcomes (git remote content, gh-call log, exit code) not implementation; each of the 4 branches (match/stale/omitted for --write-fresh; no-op/open/refresh/stand-down for the shell step) has a happy and a boundary case.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: CI job, not a runtime hot path; no loops over unbounded data; one git ls-remote + one push per drift event.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: New/changed Python files all under 300 lines. ci.yml is 552 lines but was already >300 before this change and carries no shipwright_bloat_baseline.json entry (grepped, none found) -- a pre-existing condition, not a new ratchet crossing; anti_ratchet_check.py exits 0 against this diff.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Producer: build_manifest() via --write-fresh (upstream-owned, unchanged). Consumer: the follow-up shell step, which cp's it into the tracked path and commits/pushes it. Real round-trip probe: test_traceability_regen_pr_shell.py writes a fresh JSON, executes the real shell body, and verifies the exact content lands in the pushed branch via `git show origin/<branch>:<path>` -- not a mock.
